newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sends new warning to Iraq on no-fly-zones.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sends new warning to Iraq on no-fly-zones.

text.p: The United States has sent a fresh message to Iraq telling it not to interfere with Western enforcement of no-fly-zones over Iraq, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"This demarche ... put the Iraqi government on notice that they were not to take actions that either threatened the safety of the coalition pilots or our ability to enforce the no-fly-zones -- Southern Watch and Operation Provide Comfort in the north," spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Burns told a news briefing the warning was faxed on Monday evening to the Iraqi mission at the United Nations in New York. It was the second such warning since the Iraq crisis erupted at the end of last month.

"The message that we conveyed to the Iraqis will remain in effect indefinitely. It has no expiration date. The United States will watch very closely to see whether (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein backs up his words with actions," Burns said.

"We hope that by sending this demarche that this crisis can subside," he said. Burns said the situation had "evolved significantly" since a previous message was sent to Iraq 11 days ago but did not elaborate.

After the United States fired cruise missiles at Iraq in response to a military push by Baghdad into Western-protected northern Iraq Aug. 30, Saddam said he would no longer respect the no-fly-zones and his forces fired missiles at Western planes. But the Iraqi leader later withdrew the threat.
